The verse fits Kurd on F# at only 0.721 while the chorus fits Kurd on B at 0.96, and the intro and chorus both read B, so the sections do not share one centre; the tonic also sits on an F#/B fourth-fifth split, which leaves the closest partial matches (Kurd, Bayati) unsupported.
labels.rationale: The whole piece reaches only 0.833 for Kurd on F#, and the analyzer reports no single scale and refuses a name. The section tonics disagree in a structured way: verse on F#, intro and chorus on B, with the chorus shape reaching 0.96 while the verse reaches 0.721. The cue table splits the tonic between F# (phrase endings) and B/E (most-used note, key, other voice), and 12-TET rounding would hide any quarter-tone degree that could explain the misses. Nothing in this ABC supports one name.

The declared G#m key, the commonest chord root and the verse all read Ab, and the natural-minor set fits at 0.901 in both the full and the melody-only analysis. The most-used note is Eb and the phrase endings sit on Bb, and the chorus is read on B as an Ajam shape at 0.96, so Eb, C# and B are kept as alternative tonics rather than decided away. The verse is fitted by harmonic minor, which is why that variant is listed as an alternative shape. The fit is marginal and 12-TET cannot separate this set from Bayati, so the name is consistent at low confidence only.
